answers.explanation: Push fan-out to email + SQS = SNS. night-14-sns-fanout.md decision tree. SQS is pull buffer, not multi-subscriber push.
SNS→SQS requires queue resource policy with sns.amazonaws.com + aws:SourceArn. sns-sqs-subscriber-policy.json.
Email/SMS subscriptions stay PendingConfirmation until recipient confirms. Classic exam trap.
FailedInvocations = EventBridge could not deliver to ECS target. Container exit 1 = Night 14 failure rule, not this alarm.
SNS→multiple SQS queues = fan-out pattern. One shared queue = competing consumers, not per-team copies.
EventBridge→SNS needs topic policy like SQS queue policy. sns-iceland-alerts-topic-policy.json.
SNS mobile push (APNS/FCM/GCM) via platform applications — exam awareness for fan-out to devices.
Strict order + dedup across subscribers → FIFO SNS (.fifo) with FIFO SQS subscribers.
Nights 13+14 split: SQS buffers success work; SNS pushes failure alerts. Flashcard #1.
Subscription filter policy excludes messages for that subscriber only; publish still succeeds to others.
Raw message delivery = SQS body is the published content without SNS JSON wrapper.
SNS retries Lambda on failure; use subscription DLQ for poison messages. Contrast with SQS consumer DLQ.
Worker pool with back-pressure = SQS pull. SNS pushes to all subscribers — wrong for single competing worker tier.
Cross-account SNS: topic policy on publisher side + IAM on caller. Standard integration exam pattern.
Night 13 and Night 14 are independent labs — run both setup scripts. Teardown scripts are also separate.
